source.title: Irreducibility of random polynomials: general measures
source.authors: Lior Bary-Soroker, Dimitris Koukoulopoulos, Gady Kozma
readSections: All of arXiv v3, pp. 1–65, including §§1–12, remarks, footnotes and references.
source.publicationComparison: Publisher metadata, abstract, references and numerical footnote compared; authors' 2023-05-24 PDF obtained. Publisher PDF endpoint returned HTML, not a PDF. No line-by-line identity with the typeset published proof is claimed. Source issues below refer specifically to v3.

summary: Growing-degree random integral polynomials with general independent coefficient measures: Fourier mixing modulo four primes, small-factor exclusion, positive/high-probability irreducibility, and ramified-Frobenius/random-partition Galois criteria. Partial checkpoint after a full v3 read: 130 items (15 library,3 planned,112 missing),40 definitions with120 API contracts and120 proposed tests,7 nonduplicating routes,18 source findings, and a reproducible exact-rational certificate for every consecutive coefficient interval of size≥35. Original supplier proofs, selected numerical bounds and source proof gaps remain explicit gates.

items.statement: M(n)={A∈ℤ[T]: A monic, deg A=n}, with n∈ℕ; M_p(n) is the analogous family over 𝔽_p for prime p. M(0)={1}.

items.statement: For probability masses μ_0,…,μ_{n−1} on ℤ, PM(n)(A)=∏_{j<n}μ_j(coeff_j A) on M(n). Independence is across coefficient positions, not across reductions at different primes; identical distribution is not assumed.

items.statement: For a discrete probability law p and event E of positive mass, p(·|E)=1_E p/p(E); here E={a_0≠0}. PMF.filter implements the generic normalization, and the polynomial specialization changes only μ_0.

items.name: Pointwise Fourier decay
items.statement: If |μhat_j(k/P)|≤β∈[0,1] for all P∤k and 1≤j<n, and every fraction G_p/H_p is reduced with T∤H_p, then for any q∈ℙ with ℓ_q=degH_q≥1, σ_ℙ(n;G/H)≤β^floor((n−1)/ℓ_q).
proofSteps: Every block of ℓ_q consecutive residues contains a nonzero coefficient, or H_q would divide T^JG_q.
Use distinct-prime denominators to detect a nonzero combined character.
Bound one factor in each disjoint block by β.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Characteristic function factorization
items.statement: For every X∈𝔽_ℙ((1/T)), E exp(2πiψ_ℙ(AX))=exp(2πiψ_ℙ(T^nX))∏_{j<n}μhat_j(ψ_ℙ(T^jX)).
proofSteps: Expand AX coefficientwise.
Use independence of the integer coefficients before reduction.
Separate the deterministic monic coefficient.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Fourier reduction of congruence discrepancy
items.statement: For m≥0 and r=|ℙ|, Δ_ℙ(n;m)≤(floor(m)+1)^r Σ_{0≤ℓ_p≤m,maxℓ_p≥1}δ_ℙ(n;ℓ).
proofSteps: Apply quotient additive-character orthogonality.
Reduce B/D to G/H componentwise and split off monic gcd K.
Sum ||K||^(−1) over each possible degree, bounding it by floor(m)+1.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Torus character orthogonality
items.statement: For A∈𝔽_ℙ[T], ∫_{T_ℙ}exp(2πiψ_ℙ(AX))dX=1 if A=0 and0 otherwise.
proofSteps: A nonzero coefficient of A gives a nontrivial finite-coordinate character.
Factor Haar measure into its uniform coefficients.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Haar finite-coordinate product identity
items.statement: For m≥0 and functions f_0,…,f_{m−1}:ℝ/ℤ→ℂ, ∫_{T_p}∏_{j<m}f_j(ψ_p(T^jX))dX=p^(−m)∏_{j<m}Σ_{ξ modp}f_j(ξ/p).
proofSteps: The integrand is constant on balls fixing the first m coefficients.
Sum over p^m equally weighted coefficient choices.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Polynomial Farey large-sieve inequality
items.statement: For nonnegative f_0,…,f_{m−1} on ℝ/ℤ and integer ℓ≥m/2, Σ_{H monic,degH=ℓ}Σ_{G modH,(G,H)=1}∏_{j<m}f_j(ψ_p(T^jG/H))≤p^(2ℓ−m)∏_{j<m}Σ_{ξ modp}f_j(ξ/p).
proofSteps: Use disjoint strict balls of radius p^(−2ℓ) around reduced fractions.
Integrand constant on each ball because m≤2ℓ.
Bound their union integral by the full Haar integral.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Iterated Fourier L1 estimate
items.statement: Let s≥1 integer, α≥0, γ≥1/2 and suppose Σ_{k modQ}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s≤αQ^(1−γ) for every1≤j<n,QR=P,Q>1,ℓ. If L=max_pℓ_p and m=floor((n−1)/s), then δ_ℙ(n;ℓ)≤P^max(0,L−γm) α^min(2L,m).
proofSteps: Remove the j=0 factor and incomplete block.
Hölder separates s blocks of length m; invertibility of T modulo H reindexes numerators.
Iterate Lemma6.2 over primes ordered by ℓ_p and telescope (6.5).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Approximate joint equidistribution
items.statement: For r distinct primes with product P, n≥P^4, γ≥1/2, integer1≤s≤n^(1/100), suppose Σ_{k modQ}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s≤(1−n^(−1/10))Q^(1−γ) for1≤j<n and all QR=P,Q>1,ℓ. Then Δ_ℙ(n;γn/s+n^0.88)=O_r(exp(−n^(1/10))).
proofSteps: Small L: pointwise exponential decay beats fraction count.
Middle L≤γfloor((n−1)/s): α^L supplies the decay.
Last range: P^(2+n^0.88) exp(−floor((n−1)/s)n^(−1/10)) is exponentially small.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Residue anticoncentration implies a Fourier gap
items.statement: Let P≥2 and η>0. If a probability μ onℤ has mass≤1−η in every residue class modulo every prime dividing P, then |μhat(k/P)|≤1−4η/P² for P∤k.
proofSteps: Reduce k/P to m/Q.
Expand1−|μhat|² as a double sum and use1−cos(2πt)≥8||t||².
Residue-class collision probability is at most1−η.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Fourier control bounds residue masses
items.statement: If p≥2 prime, s≥1 and Σ_{k modp}|μhat(k/p)|^s≤p^(1−γ) with γ≥1/2, then every residue mass modulo p is≤p^(−γ/s)≤2^(−1/(2s))≤1−1/(4s).
proofSteps: Fourier inversion followed by Hölder bounds each residue mass.
The final elementary inequality holds for s≥1.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See baseline, sourceIssues and completion gates.

items.name: Small irreducible factors are rare
items.statement: For support μ_j⊂[−exp(n^(1/3)),exp(n^(1/3))], ||μ_j||∞≤1−n^(−1/10) for1≤j<n, and μ_0 not concentrated at0, conditional probability given a_0≠0 of an irreducible factor of degree≤n^(1/10) is O(n^(−7/20)), with absolute constant.
proofSteps: Condition only μ_0.
Cyclotomic factors use root anticoncentration and the inverse-totient count.
Noncyclotomic factors use degree-preserving prime powers and Mahler measure to force unique sparse coefficients, then union-bound exp(n^0.54) candidates against exp(−n^0.55).

items.name: Four-prime irreducibility criterion

routes.title: Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions, Part II: random polynomials of growing degree
routes.reason: ST.0–5 organize height/discriminant-ordered number fields, Selmer averages and class-group laws; they do not plan growing-degree independent-coefficient polynomial laws. The new probability space and uniform n,H,μ estimates need new layers. PM supplies generic concentration; this route owns only its polynomial applications.
routes.brief: Build on Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions (ArithmeticStatistics), importing its counting/probability conventions without recasting these laws as discriminant-ordered fields. The endpoints are the exact statements in items29–41,44–45,52 and123; keep all conditioning, n/H ranges and absolute versus d-dependent constants. Specifically obtain probability≥1−n^(−c) for irreducibility of uniform consecutive N-element coefficient intervals when N≥35 and n≥max(n₀,(logH)^3); for2≤N≤34 obtain an absolute positive lower bound. Import the exact Fourier certificate47. For general iid laws with mass≤1−ε, the presently justified small-factor cutoff is cεn/(logH)^9 under n≥Cε^(−20000)(logH)^1000000; the paper's exponent5 remains E4, not a proved target. The l2 criterion is ||μ||₂²≤min(H^(−4/5),n^(1/16)/H)/(logH)^2. Odd-power sets, random sets and the other endpoints must retain their item-specific hypotheses and gates. Construct monic coefficient PMFs, CRT joint reductions, σ,δ,Δ, smooth/rough parts excluding T, additive statistics and conditional-law adapters with the APIs/tests in each definition. Prove small-factor exclusion, Fourier equidistribution, four-prime summability and the partition law bounds before applications. Import Finite fields, character sums, finite rings and coding interfaces (FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums) for residue duality and prime-polynomial estimates; Sieve methods, prime gaps and prime patterns (SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns) for both large sieves and Brun; Classical arithmetic, sequences, polynomials and reciprocity (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion) for sharper Mignotte and Dobrowolski; Analytic number theory, zeta functions and prime distribution (AnalyticNumberTheory) for prime and totient estimates; Probabilistic, metric and ergodic number theory (ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory) for concentration. routes.brief: Extend Galois groups of polynomials (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PolynomialGaloisGroups), importing its layers0,1,5 and9. Reuse the pinned Polynomial.Gal action, fullCycleType, factorDegrees, arithmetic Frobenius existence at ramified primes and finite-field orbit/factor theorems. Prove item100: for irreducible integral monic A and every prime p, some Galois element has cycle type obtained by merging equal parts of the mod-p factorization partition, with each merged block bounded by the maximum factor multiplicity. Do not replace this by an unramified-prime assertion. Then build the arbitrary partition-law criterion103, with all three probability premises, C,t,κ,δ and ε∈(0,δ/2). Its endpoint is ν(Merge(ρ;n^θ)∩T_n≠∅)≪(logn)^2n^(−κ(δ/4−θ/2)) uniformly0≤θ≤δ/2−ε; T_n is the union of proper transitive subgroups excluding A_n and S_n. The bound is a gated target until E12 is resolved: E₁ restricts BOTH parts to≤n/4 and cannot be used on an unrestricted auxiliary cycle. Define multiset subset and equal-part merging precisely; expose all E₁–E₅ thresholds, fixed points, multiplicity and min-support conventions. Import AnalyticNumberTheory divisor/Mertens estimates and the original primitive-group minimum-degree theorem, not an unproved Jordan-theorem shortcut. ArithmeticStatisticsPartIIRandomPolynomials supplies concrete coefficient-law instances only AFTER this arbitrary-law criterion; avoid a roadmap-level circular final theorem. Also prove the distinct-root, k-fold-irreducibility versus k-transitivity adapter and its (n−2)-fold consequence for n≥3. The construction must test identity/full cycle type, repeated mod-p factors, unit polynomial and nonseparable counterexamples. Suggested eventual modules: TauCeti/GroupTheory/Perm/RandomPartitions.lean and TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/RamifiedMerging.lean; no new Lean is claimed here.

Only the sharper sqrt(m)-exponent factor norm, its evaluation adapter, Dobrowolski and prime-power degree-drop input remain; no general Lehmer lower bound is asserted.

AN.2 owns prime counts and counts of fixed-size products of medium primes; AN.5 supplies inverse-totient/divisor/Mertens estimates. Already-built Dirichlet infinitude is imported, not replanned and not confused with PNT. The items here are source contracts with original proofs still gated.

Add the concentration function and general real independent-sum bound there as a reusable supplier; do not invent a random-polynomial-specific Kolmogorov–Rogozin theorem. The reviewed audit says generic probability/moments are built, not that this concentration estimate is built. Other consumers include bounded-digit and additive-arithmetic laws; the polynomial root projection remains in the random-polynomial Part II.
